channel.title: The Grant Desk - Artist Residencies, Journalism & Writers, US, weekly digest
channel.description: Paid open calls, fellowships and residencies in AI, tech, research, and digital and mixed-media arts, sorted into the right pile. Updated as new calls land on the desk. Filtered to: Artist Residencies, Journalism & Writers, US, weekly digest. Released weekly: each Sunday's drop carries one entry per grant added in the week before it (Sunday to Saturday). A call that closes before its drop goes out is not sent; the website lists those.

item.title: Schomburg Center Scholars-in-Residence 2027-28 (NYPL, Harlem; USD 35,000 long-term or USD 3,000 a month short-term; playwrights and creative writers eligible) (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture, The New York Public Library
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026, 23:59 EST
Award: Long-term fellowship: USD 35,000 stipend. Short-term fellowship: USD 3,000 per month for one to three months. No application fee mentioned.

Residential fellowships for work on the history, politics, literature and culture of peoples of African descent that needs the Schomburg Center's collections.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: McKnight National Residency and Commission 2027-28 (Playwrights' Center; USD 15,000 commission plus up to USD 12,250 in workshop funds) (closes 14 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Playwrights' Center, funded by the McKnight Foundation
Deadline: 14 Jan 2027, 23:59 CST
Award: USD 15,000 commission, plus up to USD 12,250 in workshop funds to develop the play, including travel and housing. No application fee mentioned.

A commission for one nationally recognised playwright from outside Minnesota to write a new play, developed through workshops at the Playwrights' Center and ending in a public reading.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Kent Cultural Alliance SFW Residency, Spring 2027 "SERVICE": six-week live-in residency in Chestertown, Maryland (USD 7,500 stipend) (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
Kent Cultural Alliance
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026, 17:00 EST
Award: USD 7,500 stipend for the six-week session, travel reimbursed up to USD 1,000, studio and gallery expenses reimbursed up to USD 1,500, and on-site housing with a private en-suite bedroom. No application fee.

A community-engaged residency on Maryland's Eastern Shore. Three artists live and work for six weeks in the Raimond Cultural Center, a restored historic house, around the theme SERVICE, working with local partners For All Seasons, the Kent County Food Pantry and Sumner Hall.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Craigardan Trillium Fellowship 2027 (residency for artists, activists and scholars of color, USD 4,600 + USD 500 honorarium) (closes 15 Dec)
item.description:
Craigardan
Deadline: 15 Dec 2026
Award: USD 4,600 fellowship toward a minimum two-week residency (covers the residency fee), plus a USD 500 honorarium. Travel, materials and personal expenses are not covered. USD 25 application fee (waivers available on request).

The Trillium Fellowship supports artists, activists and scholars of color working in any discipline who would benefit from the time and space to pursue their work or find creative retreat at Craigardan, a residency and farm in the Adirondacks.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: EFA SHIFT x Momus Residency 2027: six-month programme for New York artists who write and writers who make art (USD 2,000 honorarium) (closes 15 Dec)
item.description:
Elizabeth Foundation for the Arts (EFA Studios) with Momus
Deadline: 15 Dec 2026
Award: Artist honorarium of USD 2,000, within a six-month residency at EFA Studios with monthly critical seminars and mentoring. No application fee stated.

A new iteration of EFA's SHIFT Residency, run with the art criticism platform Momus and focused on where artistic practice meets critical writing.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Knight-Wallace Journalism Fellowships 2027-28 (University of Michigan) (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
Wallace House Center for Journalists, University of Michigan
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026, 23:59 EST
Award: USD 85,000 stipend plus USD 5,000 relocation (figures from secondary listings; confirm on the official site).

An academic-year fellowship for mid-career journalists to pursue a study project at the University of Michigan, with seminars and programming at Wallace House. DEADLINES: international applicants 1 December 2026, 11:59 pm ET; US applicants 1 February 2027. No application fee stated.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Museum of Fine Arts, Houston: Core Residency Program 2027-29 (USD 100,000 over 23 months, artists and critical writers) (closes 8 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Core Residency Program, Glassell School of Art, Museum of Fine Arts, Houston (MFAH)
Deadline: 8 Jan 2027
Award: USD 100,000 (USD 50,000 per year) plus a health and wellness stipend, private studio, and free or discounted Glassell School classes. Application fee USD 12.

Two-year residency for exceptional, highly motivated emerging artists and critical writers committed to developing a sustainable practice.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Knight Science Journalism Academic-Year Fellowship 2027-28 (MIT) (closes 9 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Knight Science Journalism Program at MIT
Deadline: 9 Jan 2027
Award: USD 87,500 stipend over 9.5 months, plus USD 5,000 for travel and housing, health insurance and a childcare subsidy. No application fee.

An academic-year fellowship at MIT for journalists covering science, health, technology or the environment, with seminars, MIT and Harvard courses and a self-directed study project.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Stigler Center: Journalists in Residence Program Spring 2027 (Chicago Booth)
item.description: Stigler Center, University of Chicago Booth School of Business · deadline 20 Sep 2026 · USD 14,000 stipend to cover living expenses over the 12-week program, plus reimbursement of economy-class airfare to and from Chicago, SEVIS and visa application fees, health insurance through UChicago, and housing guidance. The stipend is subject to up to 14 percent tax withholding for international participants, and you need sufficient funds for roughly the first month before the stipend arrives. No application fee.
